You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0030.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

args.command:
cat > /tmp/build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
import numpy as np
rw=Chem.RWMol()
# atom order: A B C D E F G H I J O1 L O2 K Ocarbonyl, MeC MeE1 MeE2 Br, Hd,Hj
spec=['C','C','C','C','C','C','C','C','C','C','O','C','O','C','O','C','C','C','Br','H','H']
for s in spec: rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom(s))
edges=[(0,1,'S'),(1,2,'S'),(2,3,'S'),(3,4,'S'),(4,5,'S'),(5,0,'S'),
       (2,15,'S'),(2,10,'S'),(10,9,'S'),(9,8,'S'),(8,7,'D'),(7,6,'S'),(6,3,'S'),
       (9,11,'S'),(11,12,'S'),(12,13,'S'),(13,8,'S'),(13,14,'D'),
       (4,16,'S'),(4,17,'S'),(5,18,'S'),(3,19,'S'),(9,20,'S')]
for a,b,t in edges:
 rw.AddBond(a,b,Chem.BondType.DOUBLE if t=='D' else Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
m=rw.GetMol(); Chem.SanitizeMol(m)
# coordinates from image: x, -y, z; all planar except explicit wedge substituents
pix={0:(194,215),1:(298,155),2:(402,215),3:(402,333),4:(298,393),5:(194,333),6:(495,410),7:(614,386),8:(667,274),9:(613,165),10:(490,147),11:(699,81),12:(805,143),13:(783,261),14:(868,322),15:(383,143),16:(246,470),17:(357,470),18:(112,380),19:(335,286),20:(612,84)}
# up y coordinates. wedge +/- z
z={15:40,16:40,17:-40,18:40,19:-40,20:-40}
conf=Chem.Conformer(m.GetNumAtoms())
for i,(x,y) in pix.items():
 conf.SetAtomPosition(i,(float(x),float(-y),float(z.get(i,0))))
m.AddConformer(conf)
# Add implicit hydrogens with positions
m=Chem.AddHs(m,addCoords=True)
# stereo from 3D depiction coordinates
Chem.AssignStereochemistryFrom3D(m, replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m, cleanIt=True, force=True)
print('stereo depiction')
for a in m.GetAtoms():
 if a.HasProp('_CIPCode'): print(a.GetIdx(),a.GetSymbol(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode'),a.GetChiralTag())
print('SMILES',Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.RemoveHs(m),isomericSmiles=True))
# Embed new conformer preserving stereo tags
m.RemoveAllConformers()
params=AllChem.ETKDGv3(); params.randomSeed=2030; params.useMacrocycleTorsions=True; params.useSmallRingTorsions=True
res=AllChem.EmbedMolecule(m,params)
print('embed',res)
if res<0: raise RuntimeError('embed failed')
mp=AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeProperties(m)
print('mmff props',bool(mp))
if mp:
 ff=AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeForceField(m,mp)
 ff.Minimize(maxIts=2000)
print('post')
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m,cleanIt=True,force=True)
for a in m.GetAtoms():
 if a.HasProp('_CIPCode'): print(a.GetIdx(),a.GetSymbol(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode'),a.GetChiralTag())
# Write explicit H XYZ
conf=m.GetConformer()
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:
 f.write(f'{m.GetNumAtoms()}\n3D structure generated from mol_0030.png; stereochemistry preserved\n')
 for a in m.GetAtoms():
  p=conf.GetAtomPosition(a.GetIdx())
  f.write(f'{a.GetSymbol():2s} {p.x: .6f} {p.y: .6f} {p.z: .6f}\n')
print('atoms',m.GetNumAtoms())
PY
python /tmp/build.py
ls -l answer.xyz
head answer.xyz

python - <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import rdMolDescriptors
m=Chem.MolFromMolFile('/dev/null') if False else Chem.MolFromSmiles('CC1(C)[C@@H](Br)CC[C@]2(C)O[C@H]3COC(=O)C3=CC[C@@H]12')
print(rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(m),m.GetNumAtoms(),rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRings(m),rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAtomStereoCenters(m))
for a in m.GetAtoms(): print(a.GetIdx(),a.GetSymbol(),a.GetTotalNumHs(),a.GetHybridization())
PY
